newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain's Alba to spend 18 mln dinars on new projects. [CORRECTED 15:12 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bahrain's Alba to spend 18 mln dinars on new projects. [CORRECTED 15:12 GMT]

text.p: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba), the Middle East's biggest aluminium producer, said on Wednesday it would spend 18 million dinars (corrects denomination of currency) on new projects to keep the smelter at the top of the industry.
An Alba statement said 14 projects including a new marine terminal and a power plant would be built in the next two to three years.

"The expenditure...will ensure the plant maintains its leading edge in the worldwide aluminium industry by further improving both the quality and quantity of its product," acting chief executive Karim Salimi said in the statement.
"These projects...show the enormous investment that Alba is undertaking to stay ahead of its competitors and to ensure it is also operating in a clean environment," he added.
Alba said on Monday it expected to produce 500,000 tonnes in 1997, buoyed by the end of an expansion project and an upgrade in the smelter.
It said a $130 million expansion project and upgrade had been completed in March, 10 weeks ahead of schedule, adding 36,500 tonnes to its annual production capacity of 460,000 tonnes.

Alba, which produced around 460,000 tonnes in 1996, is 77 percent owned by the Bahraini government and 20 percent by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. German group Breton Investments holds the rest. -- Bahrain newsroom 973-524424
